name: record_hypothesis
arguments: {"statement": "E1021K, located in the helix at residues 1008-1031 of the catalytic domain, removes a contact that holds p110delta in its inhibited state. The lysine then adds a positive charge that strengthens association with the anionic membrane surface, which increases membrane recruitment and kinase activity.", "mechanism_class": "ligand_binding", "supports": ["E2", "E4", "E7", "E14", "E16"], "would_refute": "Residue 1021 lies more than the contact distance from every lipid head group or membrane-facing ligand in all 20 experimental structures, AND the E1021K substitution does not increase membrane association in a membrane-binding assay. Either result alone would weaken it; both together would refute it.", "starting_rank": 1, "rank_rationale": "Ranked first because E2 is the only source that names this exact substitution with a mechanism, and it reports enhanced membrane association together with kinase activity. E14 and E16 support the gain-of-function direction in general. Still missing: any structure or assay that places 1021 at the membrane or lipid interface (G1, G5), and E11/E12 show residue 1021 but do not show whether it contacts a lipid. This rank is in the gain-of-function direction. The objective's loss-of-function framing conflicts with E2, E14, E16, E20 and E21, and no source supports loss of function (G3)."}
